Probe in a scratch repo (ddflow init): ddflow perf report --format json exited 0 with gates/cycle/waits/rework/comparisons/not_collected; not_collected names a section the empty log cannot support (complexity -> PM-complexity) rather than zero. Applied rules from the claim guidance: r-task-phase-needs-wave (PM-report-surfaces names phase P-perf-metrics, needs PM-report-text/PM-report-charts, wave:0), r-reuse-core (extends services/perf, no second store), r-everything-configurable (report_default_window/report_max_rows/report_width knobs in [perf_metrics] + _MIN_LABEL_H classified as an exempt structural constant), r-no-shell/r-tell-dont-discover (report names the exact next calls; svg/html written to a path with the path named), r-unavailable (a not-collected section is named, never zero), r-gemini-key-load (GEMINI_API_KEY must be exported before reviews).

Implementation complete (API already committed 4370b84ef ddflow/api/perfreport.py run_perf_report; staged: ddflow/api/__init__.py wiring, config knobs report_default_window/report_max_rows/report_width in config_sections/perf_metrics.py, report action + window/filters/format/out params on the perf Command in surfaces/declared/perfremote.py, docs/ddflow/constants-exemptions.d/ddflow.services.perf.charts.__init__.toml classifying _MIN_LABEL_H as an exempt SVG drawing threshold, tests/test_perf_report_surfaces.py 10 tests). chunk_findings.detail: JSON answers never name a next call. Given `format="json"`, `run_perf_report` sets `text` to `json.dumps(RT.to_json(report))` only and returns that as the chat body. The intent and [r-tell-dont-discover] require every answer to name the exact next CLI and MCP calls; text/md/svg/html go through `_footer`, json does not, so a machine-readable report is the one form that omits them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perfreport.py:140

chunk_findings.detail: `svg` writes one file by joining every chart with `"\n\n".join(charts.values())`. When both gate p90 and model pass-rate rows exist, that is two full SVG documents in `report-<ts>.svg`. Opening that path (the next call the footer tells the user to use) is not a single SVG document, so the file the report just wrote does not render.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perfreport.py:145

chunk_findings.detail: SVG/HTML delivery inlines the whole document with no cap: `body = f"path: {path}\n{doc}\n..."`. The stated remote/shell-less contract is file content inline only up to a bound. A report whose chart HTML/SVG exceeds that bound is still returned in full in `Outcome.text`, so the inline path is unbounded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perfreport.py:149

chunk_findings.detail: Text and markdown next-calls are built with an empty `out`: `_footer(fmt, "", win)` yields `ddflow perf report --format text --window <win> --out ` (and the same MCP form). Copying that exact command fails because `--out`/`out=` is present with no value. SVG/HTML do not have this hole; the default text path does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perfreport.py:137

chunk_findings.detail: The test never reads the JSON body for `--filters phase=P1` (`_out` is discarded) and only checks exit code 0. An implementation that ignores `phase=` and always builds the unfiltered report still passes that assertion; the later `phase=NOPE` check only covers unknown-phase refusal, not that a known phase changes `gates`/`cycle`/`waits`. So the named contract (the filter is honoured) is not falsified by any input this test runs.

chunk_findings.detail: The confirmed inline-bound defect is not fixed; the write path now drops file content entirely. Intent and PM-remote require the remote/shell-less answer to include the exact command and the SVG/HTML inline up to a bound, because the server may not share a filesystem with the user. Given `format="svg"` (or `html`), `run_perf_report` still writes `doc` to `path` but sets `body` to only `path: {path}` plus `_footer`, so `Outcome.text` never contains any of the document and there is still no bound. A host with no shared filesystem cannot open that path, and the chat answer is not the report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/perfreport.py:176

chunk_findings.detail: `_next_calls` still interpolates `out` unquoted. Given `out="my report.html"` and `win="7d"`, the CLI string is `ddflow perf report --format html --window 7d --out my report.html` (MCP: `out=my report.html`). Copying that “exact” next call splits on the space, so `--out` does not receive the path that was just written.

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP next-call generator in `ddflow/api/perfreport.py` now encloses the `out` parameter in double quotes (`out="{out}"`), but it does not escape any internal double quotes or backslashes present in the `out` string. Given an output path containing a double quote, such as `out='report"test.html'`, line 88 formats `out="report"test.html"`, producing an invalid parameter assignment that breaks parsing when copied as an MCP next call.

chunk_findings.detail: `_next_calls` now wraps `out` in double quotes but does not escape the value. Given `out='my "report".html'`, `fmt='html'`, `win='7d'`, the MCP string is `ddflow_view action=perf format=html window=7d out="my "report".html"`. A quote-aware copy of that “exact” next call ends the value at the inner `"`, so `out` is `my ` and `report".html"` is a stray token — not the path just written. The same line also breaks on a newline in `out` (`out="a\nb"` is no longer one call). `shlex.quote` on the CLI half does not have this hole.
